report.source_text: CT of the facial region with contrast showed abnormal soft tissue thickening in the region of the right side of the face with thickening and enhancement of right lacrimal gland, mild pre-septal swelling, thickening and enhancement of temporalis, lateral pterygoid and muscles of mastication on the right side. These findings were likely representing infected/inflammatory process (figure 2). There was pansinusitis with air fluid levels in bilateral maxillary sinuses and sphenoid sinuses. Pneumatised petrous temporal bone apex was visualised with fluid within it. There were ill-defined hypodensities in bilateral cerebellar hemispheres and right temporal lobe. These findings indicated possibility of an infarction.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and recent COVID-19 pneumonia presented with rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis manifesting as black facial eschar, palatal necrosis, and ophthalmoplegia. Initial CT imaging demonstrated extensive pansinusitis with orbital extension (lacrimal gland involvement, pre-septal swelling), deep facial space inflammation involving muscles of mastication, and cerebral hypodensities suggesting angioinvasion. Emergency surgical debridement including right face debridement, right eye exenteration, and bilateral functional endoscopic sinus surgery was performed. Histopathological examination of intraoperative specimens confirmed the diagnosis by demonstrating numerous aseptate fungal hyphae invading the right cheek skin, right eyeball, and nasal tissue. Postoperative CT confirmed surgical changes with interval removal of orbital structures and maturation of cerebral infarcts in the right cerebellum, hemipons, and temporal lobe.
